answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments enable autonomous agents to form a vertex of trust, where each agent's reputation serves as a ripple effect, influencing the likelihood of successful voyages of cooperation. By leveraging verifiable delay primitives, agents can ensure that malicious attempts to forge identities are thwarted by a zero-knowledge proof of sequential delay, thereby negating the expected utility of attempting to clone an agent's identity, as the probability of successful forgery decreases exponentially with the length of the delay.
